source_text: De fide contra Arianos (fragmenta) 63 Ἀρχὴ γάρ τοι τῶν καλλίστων τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὁδῶν γεγένηται ἡμῖν ὁ ἄνθρωπος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῖς κρείττοσι τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων προσάγων ἡμᾶς.
thought_title: The manhood of Christ as beginning of the fairest ways of righteousness
orientation: Eustathius is opening his argument that Christ's manhood is the starting point of the fairest paths of righteousness, leading believers to better pursuits.
pass_a_gloss: For indeed the manhood of Christ has become for us a beginning of the fairest ways of righteousness, leading us to the better pursuits.

choices.why: The glossary fixes this rendering for the human nature of Christ as the starting point of the paths of righteousness.
The glossary fixes 'way' for ὁδός; the plural here is rendered 'ways' to match the source number.
The participle is active and present, showing the manhood of Christ actively bringing believers to better pursuits.
Comparative adjective in the dative plural, modifying pursuits; 'better' preserves the comparative force.

pass_b_english: For the manhood of Christ has become for us the beginning of the fairest ways of righteousness, leading us to better pursuits.
